changes: JavaScript mask and bounded reciprocal-merge adaptation; no world-cache writes.
Compact tile merge metadata, original SelfFrame8Way lookup and coordinate variants.
General framed UV wrapping, exact anchors, independent zoom truncation, offsets and alternating plant flip are adapted in framedRules.js; compact metadata in framed.json.
Tree trunk/foliage selection and geometry, forest and background styles, palm lean and mushroom crowns are adapted in treeRules.js; world data remains read-only.

TrackUV, switch-track back layers, endcaps and sloped slices are adapted in tileContentDraws.js. Platforms and target dummies use the earlier IsFramed stored-frame dispatch from the original tile definitions and loader; the later IsPlatform adjacency branch is not used for those definitions. Browser sprites use transferable geometry or read-only dedicated scene DTOs and measured visible-region overscan.

Read-only modern entity, legacy equipment, item frame, food platter, display jar, Christmas tree, relic and dropper recipes are adapted in entityDraws.js, tileContentDraws.js and contentFrames.js; compact item scale/equipment/food/rarity metadata in itemDraws.json and rarityColors.json. Draw overload, float32 arithmetic, origin, depth, RGBA and actual missing-resource behavior are retained before browser transport.

The original IsCactus body and cold-cache initialization are adapted in cactusRules.js. cactusFrames.js computes complete eight-neighbor connected plants in original y/x cold-pass order and selects the warm-pass biome atlas in a bounded, temporary snapshot. This intentionally avoids view-history-dependent first-frame atlas selection and never writes render caches to world data. Original edge exceptions and cache-budget failures use palette fallback. Good_Cactus, Evil_Cactus and Crimson_Cactus are local-only resources; source rule, whole-plant and world-file regression do not claim desktop GPU pixel equivalence.
